events.title: Coastal Flood Watch
events.description: * WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, High astronomical tides will cause minor flooding in low lying areas around Humboldt Bay. Up to one half foot of saltwater inundation above ground level is possible near shorelines and tidal waterways. For the Coastal Flood Watch, High astronomical tides and large surf may cause major flooding in low lying areas along the Redwood/Mendocino Coast. Up to 2.5 to 3 feet of saltwater inundation above ground level is possible in low lying areas near shorelines and tidal waterways during the highest tides if storm impacts such as strong southerly winds and large surf arrive during high tide periods. * WHERE...Northern Coastal Humboldt County, especially for areas in and around Humboldt Bay. * WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, from 7 AM to 10 AM PST Saturday with high tide at 8:31 AM on Saturday at the Humboldt Bay North Spit tide gauge. For the Coastal Flood Watch, from Sunday morning through Thursday afternoon. High tide is at 9:06 AM on Sunday, 9:44 AM on Monday, 10:25 AM on Tuesday, 11:09 AM on Wednesday, 11:56 AM on Thursday, 12:48 AM on Friday at the Humboldt Bay North Spit tide gauge. Saltwater inundation will be possible 1 to 2 hours before and after high tide. * IMPACTS...Several coastal roads may be closed. Low lying property and some critical infrastructure will be inundated. Some shoreline erosion may occur.

location.region: Northern Coastal Humboldt

weather.headline: Coastal Flood Watch issued November 20 at 12:26PM PST until November 26 at 2:00PM PST by NWS Eureka CA
weather.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, High astronomical tides
will cause minor flooding in low lying areas around Humboldt
Bay. Up to one half foot of saltwater inundation above ground
level is possible near shorelines and tidal waterways. For the
Coastal Flood Watch, High astronomical tides and large surf may
cause major flooding in low lying areas along the
Redwood/Mendocino Coast. Up to 2.5 to 3 feet of saltwater
inundation above ground level is possible in low lying areas
near shorelines and tidal waterways during the highest tides if
storm impacts such as strong southerly winds and large surf
arrive during high tide periods.

* WHERE...Northern Coastal Humboldt County, especially for areas in
and around Humboldt Bay.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, from 7 AM to 10 AM PST
Saturday with high tide at 8:31 AM on Saturday at the Humboldt
Bay North Spit tide gauge. For the Coastal Flood Watch, from
Sunday morning through Thursday afternoon. High tide is at
9:06 AM on Sunday, 9:44 AM on Monday, 10:25 AM on Tuesday,
11:09 AM on Wednesday, 11:56 AM on Thursday, 12:48 AM on
Friday at the Humboldt Bay North Spit tide gauge. Saltwater
inundation will be possible 1 to 2 hours before and after high
tide.

* IMPACTS...Several coastal roads may be closed. Low lying
property and some critical infrastructure will be inundated.
Some shoreline erosion may occur.
weather.instruction:
A Coastal Flood Watch means that flooding is possible but not
imminent. Coastal residents in the watch area should begin
preparations for rising water and take appropriate action to
protect life and property.

Feet Above Ground is locally defined as feet above the Highest
Astronomical Tide or HAT.

events.title: Coastal Flood Advisory
events.description: * WHAT...For the Beach Hazards Statement, dangerous rip currents and breaking waves due to elevated surf. Elevated to high surf will likely continue into much of next week. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, moderate coastal flooding expected. For the Coastal Flood Watch, significant coastal flooding possible. * WHERE...Malibu Coast and Los Angeles County Beaches.Impacts highest across west-facing beaches, including from Santa Monica to Palos Verdes. In addition, the Long Beach/Naples area will be susceptible to the very high water levels. * WHEN...For the Beach Hazards Statement, until 3 PM PST this afternoon. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, from 3 AM Monday to 3 AM PST Wednesday. For the Coastal Flood Watch, from late Tuesday night through Thursday afternoon. * IMPACTS...There is a moderate risk for damaging flooding of sea water over some vulnerable low-lying coastal areas, especially around the time of high tide, including over beaches, roads, and structures. Significant beach erosion is possible. There is an increased risk of ocean drowning. Rip currents can pull swimmers and surfers out to sea. Waves can wash people off beaches and rocks, and capsize small boats nearshore. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Highest risk likely Wednesday and Thursday with potential for significant impacts. Additional products will likely be needed into Friday. .

location.region: Malibu Coast; Los Angeles County Beaches

weather.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued November 20 at 12:14PM PST until November 25 at 3:00AM PST by NWS Los Angeles/Oxnard CA
weather.description:
* WHAT...For the Beach Hazards Statement, dangerous rip currents
and breaking waves due to elevated surf. Elevated to high surf
will likely continue into much of next week. For the Coastal
Flood Advisory, moderate coastal flooding expected. For the
Coastal Flood Watch, significant coastal flooding possible.

* WHERE...Malibu Coast and Los Angeles County Beaches.Impacts
highest across west-facing beaches, including from Santa Monica
to Palos Verdes. In addition, the Long Beach/Naples area will be
susceptible to the very high water levels.

* WHEN...For the Beach Hazards Statement, until 3 PM PST this
afternoon. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, from 3 AM Monday to
3 AM PST Wednesday. For the Coastal Flood Watch, from late
Tuesday night through Thursday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...There is a moderate risk for damaging flooding of
sea water over some vulnerable low-lying coastal areas,
especially around the time of high tide, including over
beaches, roads, and structures. Significant beach erosion is
possible. There is an increased risk of ocean drowning. Rip
currents can pull swimmers and surfers out to sea. Waves can
wash people off beaches and rocks, and capsize small boats
nearshore.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Highest risk likely Wednesday and Thursday
with potential for significant impacts. Additional products
will likely be needed into Friday.
.
weather.instruction:
Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone property. Plan
for extra travel time as some roads may be closed.

Remain out of the water due to hazardous swimming conditions, or
stay near occupied lifeguard towers. Rock jetties can be deadly
in such conditions, stay off the rocks.

events.description: * WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, minor coastal flooding expected. For the Coastal Flood Watch, significant coastal flooding possible. * WHERE...San Diego County Coastal Areas and Orange County Coastal Areas. * WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, from 4 AM Sunday to 4 AM PST Tuesday. For the Coastal Flood Watch, from 4 AM PST Tuesday through Thursday afternoon. * IMPACTS...Numerous roads may be closed. Low lying property including homes, businesses, and some critical infrastructure may be inundated. Some shoreline erosion may occur. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Morning high tides will be on the increase next week, exceeding 7 feet by Sunday. Highest tides will be Tuesday through Thursday, peaking Wednesday. Daily high tides each morning on Tuesday through Thursday will reach 7.9-8.2 feet. Background surf on top of the tides will remain around 3-5 feet through Wednesday, but an incoming swell Wednesday into Thursday could bring notably higher surf beginning on Thursday. NOTE: Tides have been adjusted above baseline astronomical predictions based on trends in recent observations.

events.title: Coastal Flood Advisory
events.description: * WHAT...Up to 3.0 ft of inundation above ground level is possible in low-lying areas near shorelines and tidal waterways. * WHERE...Coastal North Bay Including Point Reyes National Seashore, San Francisco Peninsula Coast, Northern Monterey Bay and Southern Monterey Bay and Big Sur Coast Counties. * WHEN...From 4 AM Saturday to 4 PM PST Thursday. * IMPACTS...High tides will result in flooding of low-lying infrastructure, isolated road closures, and coastal erosion. Rising tides will bring water and waves farther up the beach than normal, restricting escape from beaches and coastal areas. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...At the San Francisco tidal gauge, high tide is expected to be 1.5 ft above normal (7.3 ft MLLW) at 8:15 AM Saturday, 2.1 ft above normal (7.9 ft MLLW) at 8:48 AM Sunday, 2.3 ft above normal (8.1 ft MLLW) at 9:25 AM Monday, 2.9 ft above normal (8.7 ft MLLW) at 10:05 AM Tuesday, 3.0 ft above normal (8.8 ft MLLW) at 10:49 AM Wednesday, and 2.6 ft above normal (8.4 ft MLLW) at 11:38 AM Thursday. These predictions include up to 1.8 ft of surge that will enhance the astronomical tide and flooding threat. High tide varies up to 90 minutes earlier or later along the Pacific Coast and through the San Francisco Bay, respectively.

events.title: Coastal Flood Advisory
events.description: * WHAT...For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 7 to 10 feet with dangerous rip currents. High surf will likely continue much of next week, peaking on Wednesday and Thursday. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, moderate coastal flooding expected. For the Coastal Flood Watch, significant coastal flooding possible. * WHERE...San Luis Obispo County Beaches, Santa Barbara County Central Coast Beaches, Ventura County Beaches, Malibu Coast and Los Angeles County Beaches. * WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, from 3 AM Monday to 3 AM PST Wednesday. For the Coastal Flood Watch, from late Tuesday night through Thursday afternoon. * IMPACTS...There is a moderate risk for damaging flooding of sea water over some vulnerable low-lying coastal areas, especially around the time of high tide, including over beaches, roads, and structures. Significant beach erosion is possible. There is an increased risk for ocean drowning. Rip currents can pull swimmers and surfers out to sea. Large breaking waves can cause injury, wash people off beaches and rocks, and capsize small boats near shore. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Highest risk likely Wednesday and Thursday with potential for significant impacts. Additional products will likely be needed into Friday.

events.title: Coastal Flood Watch
events.description: * WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, High astronomical tides will cause minor flooding in low lying areas around Humboldt Bay. Up to one half foot of saltwater inundation above ground level is possible near shorelines and tidal waterways. For the Coastal Flood Watch, High astronomical tides and large surf may cause major flooding in low lying areas along the Redwood/Mendocino Coast. Up to 2.5 to 3 feet of saltwater inundation above ground level is possible in low lying areas near shorelines and tidal waterways during the highest tides if storm impacts such as strong southerly winds and large surf arrive during high tide periods. * WHERE...Northern Coastal Humboldt County, especially for areas in and around Humboldt Bay. * WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, from 7 AM to 10 AM PST Saturday with high tide at 8:31 AM on Saturday at the Humboldt Bay North Spit tide gauge. events.description: * WHAT...For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 7 to 10 feet with dangerous rip currents. For the Coastal Flood Watch, significant coastal flooding possible. * WHERE...San Luis Obispo County Beaches, Santa Barbara County Central Coast Beaches, Ventura County Beaches, Malibu Coast and Los Angeles County Beaches. * WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, from 3 AM Monday to 3 AM PST Wednesday. Large breaking waves can cause injury, wash people off beaches and rocks, and capsize small boats near shore. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Highest risk likely Wednesday and Thursday with potential for significant impacts. Additional products will likely be needed into Friday.

Up to one half to one foot of saltwater inundation above ground level is possible in low lying areas near shorelines and tidal waterways. * WHERE...Coastal Del Norte, Southwestern Humboldt and Coastal Mendocino Counties. * WHEN...From Tuesday morning through Thursday afternoon. . * IMPACTS...Several coastal roads may be closed. Low lying property and some critical infrastructure will be inundated. Some shoreline erosion may occur.

location.region: Coastal Del Norte; Southwestern Humboldt; Coastal Mendocino

weather.headline: Coastal Flood Watch issued November 21 at 9:57AM PST until November 26 at 2:00PM PST by NWS Eureka CA
weather.description:

to major flooding in low lying areas along the Redwood/Mendocino
Coast. Up to one half to one foot of saltwater inundation above
ground level is possible in low lying areas near shorelines and
tidal waterways.

* WHERE...Coastal Del Norte, Southwestern Humboldt and Coastal

* WHEN...From Tuesday morning through Thursday afternoon. .

weather.instruction:
A Coastal Flood Watch means that flooding is possible but not
imminent. Coastal residents in the watch area should begin
preparations for rising water and take appropriate action to
protect life and property.

Feet Above Ground is locally defined as feet above the Highest
Astronomical Tide or HAT.

events.title: Coastal Flood Advisory
events.description: * WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, minor coastal flooding expected. For the Coastal Flood Watch, significant coastal flooding possible. * WHERE...San Diego County Coastal Areas and Orange County Coastal Areas. * WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, from 4 AM Sunday to 4 AM PST Tuesday. For the Coastal Flood Watch, from 4 AM PST Tuesday through Thursday afternoon. * IMPACTS...Numerous roads may be closed. Low lying property including homes, businesses, and some critical infrastructure may be inundated. Some shoreline erosion may occur. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Morning high tides will be on the increase next week, exceeding 7 feet by Sunday. Highest tides will be Tuesday through Thursday, peaking Wednesday. Daily high tides each morning on Tuesday through Thursday will reach 7.9-8.2 feet, likely re-breaking the all time tidal records set back in late October. Background surf on top of the tides will remain around 3-5 feet through Wednesday, but an incoming swell Wednesday into Thursday could bring notably higher surf beginning on Thursday. Uncertainty remains in exact surf heights at this time, but look to be 6-8 feet with sets up to 10 feet on west-facing beaches. NOTE: Tides have been adjusted above baseline astronomical predictions based on trends in recent observations.

location.region: San Diego County Coastal Areas; Orange County Coastal

events.title: Coastal Flood Watch
events.description: * WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, minor coastal flooding expected. For the Coastal Flood Watch, significant coastal flooding possible. Most susceptible time of flooding will be around the time of the morning high tides between about 730 AM and 930 AM. * WHERE...Ventura County Beaches. * WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, from 3 AM Monday to 3 AM PST Wednesday. For the Coastal Flood Watch, from late Tuesday night through Thursday afternoon. * IMPACTS...There is a moderate risk for damaging flooding of sea water over some vulnerable low-lying coastal areas, especially around the time of high tide, including over beaches, roads, and structures. Significant beach erosion is possible. There is an increased risk for ocean drowning. Rip currents can pull swimmers and surfers out to sea. Large breaking waves can cause injury, wash people off beaches and rocks, and capsize small boats near shore. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Highest risk likely Wednesday and Thursday with potential for significant impacts. Elevated to high surf is expected much of the week, with even the possibility of warning- level surf at times from Wednesday afternoon into Thursday. Additional products will likely be needed into Friday.

Most susceptible time of flooding will be around the time of the morning high tides between about 730 AM and 930 AM. * WHERE...Ventura County Beaches. * WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, from 3 AM Monday to 3 AM PST Wednesday. For the Coastal Flood Watch, from late Tuesday night through Thursday afternoon. * IMPACTS...There is a moderate risk for damaging flooding of sea water over some vulnerable low-lying coastal areas, especially around the time of high tide, including over beaches, roads, and structures. Significant beach erosion is possible. There is an increased risk for ocean drowning. Rip currents can pull swimmers and surfers out to sea. Large breaking waves can cause injury, wash people off beaches and rocks, and capsize small boats near shore. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Highest risk likely Wednesday and Thursday with potential for significant impacts. Elevated to high surf is expected much of the week, with even the possibility of warning- level surf at times from Wednesday afternoon into Thursday. Additional products will likely be needed into Friday.

location.region: Ventura County Beaches

events.description: * WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, tidal overflow flooding expected. For the Coastal Flood Watch, coastal flooding possible. * WHERE...North and Central Coast of Oregon, and South Washington Coast. * WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, from 4 AM Sunday to 4 AM PST Tuesday. Coastal residents in the warned area should be alert for rising water, and take appropriate action to protect life and property. A Coastal Flood Watch means that conditions favorable for flooding are expected to develop. Coastal residents should be alert for later statements or warnings, and take action to protect property.

events.title: Coastal Flood Watch
events.description: * WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, minor coastal flooding expected. For the Coastal Flood Watch, significant coastal flooding possible. * WHERE...San Diego County Coastal Areas and Orange County Coastal Areas. * WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, from 4 AM Sunday to 4 AM PST Tuesday. For the Coastal Flood Watch, from 4 AM PST Tuesday through Thursday afternoon. * IMPACTS...Numerous roads may be closed. Low lying property including homes, businesses, and some critical infrastructure may be inundated. Some shoreline erosion may occur. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Morning high tides will be on the increase next week, exceeding 7 feet by Sunday. Highest tides will be Tuesday through Thursday, peaking Wednesday. Daily high tides each morning on Tuesday through Thursday will reach 7.9-8.2 feet, likely re-breaking the all time tidal records set back in late October. Background surf on top of the tides will remain around 3- 5 feet through Wednesday, but an incoming swell Wednesday into Thursday could bring notably higher surf beginning on Thursday. Uncertainty remains in exact surf heights at this time, but look to be 6-8 feet with sets up to 10 feet on west-facing beaches.

events.title: Coastal Flood Advisory
events.description: * WHAT...Up to 2.8 ft of inundation above ground level is possible in low-lying areas near shorelines and tidal waterways. * WHERE...Pacific Ocean Coast. * WHEN...Through 4 PM PST Thursday. * IMPACTS...High tides will result in flooding of low-lying infrastructure, isolated road closures, and coastal erosion. Rising tides will bring water and waves farther up the beach than normal, restricting escape from beaches and coastal areas. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...These predictions are approaching the highest tide ever recorded. At the San Francisco tide gauge, high tide is expected to be 2.0 ft above normal (7.8 ft MLLW) at 8:48 AM Sunday, 2.2 ft above normal (8.0 ft MLLW) at 9:25 AM Monday, 2.6 ft above normal (8.4 ft MLLW) at 10:05 AM Tuesday, 2.8 ft above normal (8.6 ft MLLW) at 10:49 AM Wednesday, and 2.4 ft above normal (8.2 ft MLLW) at 11:38 AM Thursday. These predictions include up to 1.6 ft of surge that will enhance the astronomical tide and flooding threat. High tide varies up to 90 minutes earlier or later along the Pacific Coast and through the San Francisco Bay, respectively.

location.region: Coastal North Bay Including Point Reyes National Seashore; San Francisco Peninsula Coast; Northern Monterey Bay; Southern Monterey Bay and Big Sur Coast

events.title: Coastal Flood Advisory
events.description: * WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, minor coastal flooding expected. For the Coastal Flood Watch, significant coastal flooding possible. * WHERE...San Diego County Coastal Areas and Orange County Coastal Areas. * WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, from 4 AM Sunday to 4 AM PST Tuesday. For the Coastal Flood Watch, from 4 AM PST Tuesday through Thursday afternoon. * IMPACTS...Numerous roads may be closed. Low lying property including homes, businesses, and some critical infrastructure may be inundated. Some shoreline erosion may occur. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Morning high tides will be on the increase this upcoming week. Highest tides will be Tuesday through Thursday, peaking Wednesday. Daily high tides each morning on Tuesday through Thursday will reach 7.9-8.2 feet, likely re- breaking the all time tidal records set back in late October. Background surf on top of the tides will remain around 3-5 feet through Wednesday, but an incoming swell Wednesday into Thursday could bring notably higher surf beginning on Thursday. Uncertainty remains in exact surf heights at this time, but look to be 6-8 feet with sets up to 10 feet on west-facing beaches.

events.title: Coastal Flood Watch
events.description: * WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, tidal overflow flooding expected. For the Coastal Flood Watch, coastal flooding possible. * WHERE...North and Central Coast of Oregon, and South Washington Coast. * WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, from 4 AM Sunday to 4 AM PST Tuesday. For the Coastal Flood Watch, from late Monday night through late Thursday night. * IMPACTS...Major flooding, up to two feet above ground level, during high tides is possible along the immediate coast as well as low lying areas near bays, sloughs, and the lower reaches of the coastal rivers. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...A Coastal Flood Advisory means that tidal overflow flooding of low-lying areas is expected due to high tides. Coastal residents in the warned area should be alert for rising water, and take appropriate action to protect life and property. A Coastal Flood Watch means that more significant coastal flooding due to a combination of high surf and high tides is possible. Coastal residents should be alert for later statements or warnings, and take action to protect property.

events.title: Coastal Flood Warning
events.description: * WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, up to 2.0 ft of inundation above ground level is possible in low-lying areas near shorelines and tidal waterways. For the Coastal Flood Warning, significant coastal flooding with up to 2.8 feet of inundation above ground level is possible in low-lying areas near shorelines and tidal waterways. * WHERE...San Francisco and San Pablo Bay Shorelines. * WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 6 AM PST Monday. For the Coastal Flood Warning, from 6 AM Monday to 4 PM PST Thursday. * IMPACTS...High tides will result in flooding of low-lying infrastructure, numerous road closures, and coastal erosion. Rising tides will bring water and waves farther up the beach than normal, restricting escape from beaches and coastal areas. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...These predictions are approaching the highest tide ever recorded. At the San Francisco tide gauge, high tide is expected to be 2.2 ft above normal (8.0 ft MLLW) at 9:25 AM Monday, 2.6 ft above normal (8.4 ft MLLW) at 10:05 AM Tuesday, 2.8 ft above normal (8.6 ft MLLW) at 10:49 AM Wednesday, and 2.4 ft above normal (8.2 ft MLLW) at 11:38 AM Thursday. These predictions include up to 1.6 ft of surge that will enhance the astronomical tide and flooding threat. High tide varies up to 90 minutes earlier or later along the Pacific Coast and through the San Francisco Bay, respectively.

events.description: * WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Warning, High astronomical tides and storm surge will cause moderate flooding in low lying areas along the Humboldt Bay Coast. Up to 1.5 to 2.0 feet of saltwater inundation above ground level is possible in low lying areas near shorelines and tidal waterways. Between 9.5 and 9.8 feet MLLW at the North Spit tide gauge is predicted. For the Coastal Flood Watch, High astronomical tides and large surf with storm surge may cause moderate flooding in low lying areas along the Redwood/Mendocino Coast. Up to one foot of saltwater inundation above ground level is possible in low lying areas near shorelines and tidal waterways. * WHERE...Northern Coastal Humboldt County. * WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Warning, from 7 AM to noon PST Monday. For the Coastal Flood Watch, from Monday afternoon through Thursday afternoon. High tide is at 9:44 AM at the Humboldt Bay North Spit tide gauge. Saltwater inundation will be possible 1 to 2 hours before and after high tide. * IMPACTS...Several coastal roads may be closed. Low lying property and some critical infrastructure will be inundated. These impacts will include, but not limited to, roadways in King Salmon and the Arcata bottoms/sections of highway 101 Shoreline erosion will occur. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Expect continued increases in high tide water levels through the coming work week with the tide peaking on Wednesday. Prepare now and pay attention to official guidance on shelters and or resources available to the public..

events.title: Coastal Flood Advisory
events.description: * WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, minor coastal flooding. For the Coastal Flood Warning, significant coastal flooding expected. * WHERE...San Diego County Coastal Areas and Orange County Coastal Areas. * WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 4 AM PST Tuesday. For the Coastal Flood Warning, from 4 AM Tuesday to 1 PM PST Friday. Most susceptible time of flooding will be around the time of the morning high tide, with peak tides trending from 7 AM on Monday to 10 AM on Friday. * IMPACTS...Numerous roads may be closed. Low lying property including homes, businesses, and some critical infrastructure will be inundated. Some shoreline erosion will occur. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...King tides peak Tuesday through Wednesday, reaching 7.9-8.3 feet, likely re-breaking the all-time tidal records set back in late October. Background surf on top of the tides will remain around 3-5 feet through Wednesday, but an incoming swell Wednesday into Thursday will bring a sharp increase to the surf by Thursday morning's high tide. Breaking waves may reach 6-8 feet with sets up to 10 feet on west-facing beaches. Surf then moderates some into Friday, but still looks to be around 5-8 feet.

weather.description:

* WHERE...East facing reefs of the Marianas.

* WHEN...Through Thursday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...A building trade-wind swell will produce a

escape, face the shore and call or wave for help.

events.title: High Surf Advisory
events.description: * WHAT...For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 9 to 11 feet building to 15 to 22 feet Wednesday with dangerous rip currents. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, minor to moderate coastal flooding expected. For the Coastal Flood Watch, significant coastal flooding possible. Most susceptible time of flooding will be around the time of the morning high tides between about 800 AM and 1000 AM, especially Wednesday and Thursday. * WHERE...San Luis Obispo County Beaches and Santa Barbara County Central Coast Beaches. * WHEN...For the High Surf Advisory, from 6 AM Sunday to 3 PM PST Thursday. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, from 3 AM Monday to 3 AM PST Wednesday. For the Coastal Flood Watch, from late Tuesday night through Thursday afternoon. * IMPACTS...There is the potential for damaging flooding of sea water over some vulnerable low-lying coastal areas, especially around the time of high tide, including over beaches, roads, and coastal structures including piers. Significant beach erosion is likely. There is an increased risk for ocean drowning. Rip currents can pull swimmers and surfers out to sea. Large breaking waves can cause injury, wash people off beaches and rocks, and capsize small boats near shore. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Highest risk likely Wednesday and Thursday with potential for significant impacts. The High Surf Advisory will likely be needed to be upgraded to a High Surf Warning for Wednesday and Thursday when there will be the potential for damaging surf. Additional products will likely be needed into Friday.

location.region: San Luis Obispo County Beaches; Santa Barbara County Central Coast Beaches

weather.headline: High Surf Advisory issued November 22 at 3:04PM PST until November 26 at 3:00PM PST by NWS Los Angeles/Oxnard CA
weather.description:
* WHAT...For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 9 to
11 feet building to 15 to 22 feet Wednesday with dangerous rip
currents. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, minor to moderate
coastal flooding expected. For the Coastal Flood Watch,
significant coastal flooding possible. Most susceptible time of
flooding will be around the time of the morning high tides
between about 800 AM and 1000 AM, especially Wednesday and
Thursday.

* WHERE...San Luis Obispo County Beaches and Santa Barbara
County Central Coast Beaches.

* WHEN...For the High Surf Advisory, from 6 AM Sunday to 3 PM
PST Thursday. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, from 3 AM Monday
to 3 AM PST Wednesday. For the Coastal Flood Watch, from late
Tuesday night through Thursday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...There is the potential for damaging flooding of sea
water over some vulnerable low-lying coastal areas, especially
around the time of high tide, including over beaches, roads, and
coastal structures including piers. Significant beach erosion
is likely. There is an increased risk for ocean drowning. Rip
currents can pull swimmers and surfers out to sea. Large
breaking waves can cause injury, wash people off beaches and
rocks, and capsize small boats near shore.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Highest risk likely Wednesday and Thursday
with potential for significant impacts. The High Surf Advisory
will likely be needed to be upgraded to a High Surf Warning for
Wednesday and Thursday when there will be the potential for
damaging surf. Additional products will likely be needed into
Friday.
weather.instruction:
Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone property. Plan
for extra travel time as some roads may be closed.

Remain out of the water due to dangerous surf conditions, or stay

events.title: Coastal Flood Watch
events.description: * WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Warning, High astronomical tides and storm surge will cause moderate flooding in low lying areas along the Humboldt Bay Coast. Up to 1.5 to 2.0 feet of saltwater inundation above ground level is possible in low lying areas near shorelines and tidal waterways. Between 9.3 and 9.8 feet MLLW at the North Spit tide gauge is predicted. For the Coastal Flood Watch, High astronomical tides and large surf with storm surge may cause moderate flooding in low lying areas along the Redwood/Mendocino Coast. Up to one foot of saltwater inundation above ground level is possible in low lying areas near shorelines and tidal waterways. * WHERE...Northern Coastal Humboldt County. * WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Warning, from 7 AM to noon PST Monday. For the Coastal Flood Watch, from Monday afternoon through Thursday afternoon. High tide is at 9:44 AM at the Humboldt Bay North Spit tide gauge. Saltwater inundation will be possible 1 to 2 hours before and after high tide. * IMPACTS...Several coastal roads may be closed. Low lying property and some critical infrastructure will be inundated. These impacts will include, but not limited to, roadways in King Salmon and the Arcata bottoms/sections of highway 101 Shoreline erosion will occur. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Expect continued increases in high tide water levels through the coming work week with the tide peaking on Wednesday. Prepare now and pay attention to official guidance on shelters and or resources available to the public.

events.description: * WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, Up to 2.0 ft of inundation above ground level is possible in low-lying areas near shorelines and tidal waterways. For the Coastal Flood Warning, significant coastal flooding with up to 2.8 feet of inundation above ground level is possible in low-lying areas near shorelines and tidal waterways. For the High Surf Warning, Dangerously large breaking waves of 20 to 30 feet. * WHERE...San Francisco County. * WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 6 AM PST Monday. For the Coastal Flood Warning, from 6 AM Monday to 4 PM PST Thursday. For the High Surf Warning, from midnight Tuesday night to midnight PST Wednesday night. * IMPACTS...High tides will result in flooding of low-lying infrastructure, numerous road closures, and coastal erosion. Rising tides will bring water and waves farther up the beach than normal, restricting escape from beaches and coastal areas. Dangerously large breaking waves can overpower swimmers, pulling people into the sea from beaches, jetties, and rocks resulting in significant physical injury and increasing the risk of drowning. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...These predictions are approaching the highest tide ever recorded. At the San Francisco tide gauge, high tide is expected to be 2.2 ft above normal (8.0 ft MLLW) at 9:25 AM Monday, 2.6 ft above normal (8.4 ft MLLW) at 10:05 AM Tuesday, 2.8 ft above normal (8.6 ft MLLW) at 10:49 AM Wednesday, and 2.4 ft above normal (8.2 ft MLLW) at 11:38 AM Thursday. These predictions include up to 1.6 ft of surge that will enhance the astronomical tide and flooding threat. High tide varies up to 90 minutes earlier or later along the Pacific Coast and through the San Francisco Bay, respectively.

events.title: Coastal Flood Warning
events.description: * WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, higher than normal astronomical tides (King Tides) are expected to bring up to 2.4 ft of inundation above ground level in low-lying areas near shorelines and tidal waterways on Monday. For the Coastal Flood Warning, higher than normal astronomical tides (King Tides) combined with storm surge from large surf are expected to bring up to 3.1 ft of inundation above ground level Tuesday and Wednesday, with up to 2.6 ft of inundation expected on Thursday. * WHERE...Beaches and low lying areas along the shore lines of Douglas, Coos and Curry Counties. This includes the communities of North Bend, Charleston, Port Orford, Gold Beach, and Coos Bay. Coastal flooding is expected to impact portions of Highway 101 around Gold Beach, Coos Bay, and Reedsport. * WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, from 7 AM to 4 PM PST Monday. For the Coastal Flood Warning, from 7 AM Tuesday to 7 PM PST Thursday. * IMPACTS...Numerous roads may be closed. Low lying property including homes, businesses, and some critical infrastructure will be inundated. Some shoreline erosion will occur. This event is expected see similar impacts to what occurred on January 3rd, 2026. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...The worst conditions are expected to be during the high tide periods in the late morning/early afternoon. This is especially so for Tuesday and Wednesday as storm activity brings large breaking surf heights of 23 to 28 ft and adds storm surge to the water levels. Storm activity lessens on Thursday, but King Tides will still be present, which will likely continue inundation impacts. At the Charleston, OR tide gauge, high tide is expected to be at 10:09 AM Monday, at 10:51 AM Tuesday, at 11:35 AM Wednesday, and at 12:23 PM Thursday.

events.title: Coastal Flood Watch
events.description: * WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Watch, High astronomical tides and large surf with storm surge may cause moderate flooding in low lying areas along the Redwood/Mendocino Coast. Up to one foot of saltwater inundation above ground level is possible in low lying areas near shorelines and tidal waterways. * WHERE...Coastal Del Norte, Southwestern Humboldt and Coastal Mendocino Counties. * WHEN...From Tuesday morning through Thursday afternoon during periods of high tide. * IMPACTS...Several coastal roads may be closed. Low lying property and some critical infrastructure will be inundated. Some shoreline erosion may occur. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Expect continued increases in high tide water levels through the coming work week with the tide peaking on Wednesday. Prepare now and pay attention to official guidance on shelters and or resources available to the public.

location.region: Coastal Del Norte; Southwestern Humboldt; Coastal Mendocino

weather.headline: Coastal Flood Watch issued November 22 at 10:49PM PST until November 26 at 2:00PM PST by NWS Eureka CA
weather.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Watch, High astronomical tides
and large surf with storm surge may cause moderate flooding in
low lying areas along the Redwood/Mendocino Coast. Up to one
foot of saltwater inundation above ground level is possible in
low lying areas near shorelines and tidal waterways.

* WHERE...Coastal Del Norte, Southwestern Humboldt and Coastal
Mendocino Counties.

* WHEN...From Tuesday morning through Thursday afternoon during
periods of high tide.

* IMPACTS...Several coastal roads may be closed. Low lying
property and some critical infrastructure will be inundated.
Some shoreline erosion may occur.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Expect continued increases in high tide
water levels through the coming work week with the tide
peaking on Wednesday. Prepare now and pay attention to
official guidance on shelters and or resources available to
the public.
weather.instruction:
A Coastal Flood Watch means that flooding is possible but not
imminent. Coastal residents in the watch area should begin
preparations for rising water and take appropriate action to
protect life and property.

Feet Above Ground is locally defined as feet above the Highest
Astronomical Tide or HAT.

location.region: Guam; Rota; Tinian; Saipan

weather.headline: Rip Current Statement issued November 23 at 3:42PM ChST until November 26 at 3:00PM ChST by NWS Tiyan GU
weather.description:
* WHAT...Dangerous rip currents.

* WHERE...East facing reefs of the Marianas.

* WHEN...Through Thursday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away
from shore into deeper water.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...A trade-wind swell will continue to produce
a high risk of rip currents along east-facing reefs. Surf along
east-facing reefs will also be elevated with the rip current
risk along north-facing reefs also elevated.
weather.instruction:
Rip currents will be life threatening. If caught in a rip
current, relax and float. Don't swim against the current. If
able, swim in a direction following the shoreline. If unable to
escape, face the shore and call or wave for help.

events.title: Coastal Flood Advisory
events.description: * WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, minor coastal flooding. For the Coastal Flood Warning, significant coastal flooding expected. * WHERE...San Diego County Coastal Areas and Orange County Coastal Areas. * WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 4 AM PST Tuesday. For the Coastal Flood Warning, from 4 AM Tuesday to 1 PM PST Friday. Most susceptible time of flooding will be around the time of the morning high tide, with peak tides trending from 7 AM on Monday to 10 AM on Friday. * IMPACTS...Numerous roads may be closed. Low lying property including homes, businesses, and some critical infrastructure will be inundated. Some shoreline erosion will occur. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...King tides peak Tuesday through Wednesday, reaching 7.9-8.3 feet, likely re-breaking the all- time tidal records set back in late October. Background surf on top of the tides will remain around 3-5 feet through Wednesday, but an incoming swell Wednesday into Thursday will bring a sharp increase to the surf by Thursday morning's high tide. Breaking waves may reach 6-8 feet with sets up to 10 feet on west-facing beaches. Surf then moderates some into Friday, but still looks to be around 5-8 feet.

events.title: Special Weather Statement
events.description: An approaching storm system late Monday will bring increasing moisture and colder temperatures to the region. Overnight lows are expected to fall below freezing area-wide, allowing for isolated to scattered snow showers to develop overnight and continue into Tuesday morning. Any accumulations are expected to remain light, with little to no impacts anticipated. However, a few slick spots cannot be ruled out, particularly on bridges and overpasses. Motorists are encouraged to use caution during the morning commute Tuesday.

events.title: Special Weather Statement
events.description: The combination of an upper level storm system, increasing moisture and temperatures in the 30s may produce a few hours of light snow mainly west of a Sterling City to Throckmorton line Tuesday morning. Expect little to no accumulation of snowfall. However, there is a low chance of local accumulations around 1/2 of an inch which may cause a few slick spots on roads. The rest of west central Texas will only see rain showers Tuesday morning. Keep up with the latest weather information this week. Also, expect colder temperatures across the area. A widespread freeze is expected Wednesday morning with lows in the mid to upper 20s, possibly a few degrees colder in low lying areas and river valleys. Highs will only be in the 40s Tuesday. Please prepare for the colder weather.

events.title: Coastal Flood Watch
events.description: * WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Warning, significant coastal flooding expected. Inundation of 2.5 to 3.5 feet above ground level is possible Tuesday along shorelines and low- lying coastal areas. For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves along the coast. For the first Coastal Flood Watch, significant coastal flooding possible Wednesday with inundation up to 2.5 to 3.5 feet. For the second Coastal Flood Watch, significant coastal flooding possible Thursday with inundation up to 2.5 to 3.5 feet. * WHERE...Northern Washington Coast zone. * WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Warning, from 8 AM to 3 PM PST Tuesday. For the High Surf Advisory, from 10 AM Tuesday to 4 PM PST Wednesday. For the first Coastal Flood Watch, from late Tuesday night through Wednesday afternoon. For the second Coastal Flood Watch, from late Wednesday night through Thursday afternoon. * IMPACTS...Significant coastal flooding due to high tides and storm surge is expected. This is expected to lead to numerous road closures. Low lying property including homes, businesses, and some critical infrastructure may be inundated. Shoreline erosion or damage may occur. Large breaking waves can knock people off their feet, move driftwood and debris, and crash over rocks and jetties. People can be injured or drown while observing the ocean. Localized beach and coastal erosion is expected.

events.title: Coastal Flood Advisory
events.description: * WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, higher than normal astronomical tides (King Tides) are expected to bring up to 2.4 ft of inundation above ground level in low-lying areas near shorelines and tidal waterways today. For the Coastal Flood Warning, higher than normal astronomical tides (King Tides) combined with storm surge from large surf (breaking wave heights of 23 to 28 ft) are expected to bring up to 3.3 ft of inundation above ground level Tuesday and Wednesday, with up to 2.8 ft of inundation expected on Thursday. * WHERE...Beaches and low lying areas along the shore lines of Douglas, Coos and Curry Counties. This includes the communities of North Bend, Charleston, Port Orford, Gold Beach, and Coos Bay. Coastal flooding is expected to impact portions of Highway 101 around Gold Beach, Coos Bay, and Reedsport. * WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 4 PM PST this afternoon. For the Coastal Flood Warning, from 7 AM Tuesday to 7 PM PST Thursday. * IMPACTS...Numerous roads may be closed. Low lying property including homes, businesses, and some critical infrastructure will be inundated. Some shoreline erosion will occur. This event is expected see similar impacts to what occurred on January 3rd, 2026. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...The worst conditions are expected to be during the high tide periods in the late morning/early afternoon. Storm activity lessens on Thursday, but King Tides will still be present, which will likely continue inundation impacts. At the Charleston, OR tide gauge, high tide is expected to be at 10:09 AM today, at 10:51 AM Tuesday, at 11:35 AM Wednesday, and at 12:23 PM Thursday.

events.title: Coastal Flood Advisory
events.description: * WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, minor to moderate coastal flooding. For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 6 to 11 feet with dangerous rip currents. For the Coastal Flood Watch, significant coastal flooding possible. * WHERE...Malibu Coast and Los Angeles County Beaches. Highest surf along west facing beaches. * WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 8 AM PST Wednesday. For the High Surf Advisory, from 6 AM Wednesday to 9 PM PST Thursday. For the Coastal Flood Watch, from Wednesday morning through Thursday morning. * IMPACTS...There is a moderate risk for damaging flooding of sea water over some vulnerable low-lying coastal areas, especially around the time of high tide, including over beaches (especially from Santa Monica to Palos Verdes and Malibu), roads, and structures. Significant beach erosion is possible. There is an increased risk for ocean drowning. Rip currents can pull swimmers and surfers out to sea. Large breaking waves can cause injury, wash people off beaches and rocks, and capsize small boats near shore. Extremely high tides may cause dock damage and seawater spillage over low lying areas inside of harbor areas (such as Naples in Long Beach). * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Extremely high tides of 8.1-8.4 feet will likely peak between 7am and 11am. An upgrade to a Coastal Flood Warning would likely come by Tuesday. Coastal Flood and High Surf Advisories are likely to follow the expiration of the respective warnings if they are issued.

location.region: Malibu Coast; Los Angeles County Beaches

weather.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued November 23 at 12:06PM PST until November 25 at 8:00AM PST by NWS Los Angeles/Oxnard CA
weather.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, minor to moderate coastal
flooding. For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 6
to 11 feet with dangerous rip currents. For the Coastal Flood
Watch, significant coastal flooding possible.

* WHERE...Malibu Coast and Los Angeles County Beaches. Highest
surf along west facing beaches.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 8 AM PST
Wednesday. For the High Surf Advisory, from 6 AM Wednesday to
9 PM PST Thursday. For the Coastal Flood Watch, from Wednesday
morning through Thursday morning.

* IMPACTS...There is a moderate risk for damaging flooding of sea
water over some vulnerable low-lying coastal areas, especially
around the time of high tide, including over beaches (especially
from Santa Monica to Palos Verdes and Malibu), roads, and
structures. Significant beach erosion is possible. There is an
increased risk for ocean drowning. Rip currents can pull
swimmers and surfers out to sea. Large breaking waves can cause
injury, wash people off beaches and rocks, and capsize small
boats near shore. Extremely high tides may cause dock damage and
seawater spillage over low lying areas inside of harbor areas
(such as Naples in Long Beach).

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Extremely high tides of 8.1-8.4 feet will
likely peak between 7am and 11am. An upgrade to a Coastal Flood
Warning would likely come by Tuesday. Coastal Flood and High
Surf Advisories are likely to follow the expiration of the
respective warnings if they are issued.
weather.instruction:
Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone property. Plan
for extra travel time as some roads may be closed.

Remain out of the water due to dangerous surf conditions, or stay
near occupied lifeguard towers. Rock jetties can be deadly in
such conditions, stay off the rocks.
weather.areaDesc: Malibu Coast; Los Angeles County Beaches

events.title: High Surf Advisory
events.description: * WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, minor to moderate coastal flooding. For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 8 to 12 feet with dangerous rip currents. For the Coastal Flood Warning, significant coastal flooding expected. For the High Surf Warning, large damaging breaking waves of 15 to 22 feet with dangerous rip currents are expected. * WHERE...San Luis Obispo County Beaches and Santa Barbara County Central Coast Beaches. Highest surf along west facing beaches. * WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 6 AM PST Wednesday. For the Coastal Flood Warning, from 6 AM Wednesday to noon PST Thursday. For the High Surf Warning, from 6 AM Wednesday to noon PST Thursday. * IMPACTS...Damaging flooding of sea water is likely over some vulnerable low-lying coastal areas, especially around the time of high tide, including over beaches (especially Oceano Dunes, Pismo Beach, and Morro Bay), roads, and structures. Significant beach erosion is expected. events.title: Coastal Flood Watch
events.description: * WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Watch, High astronomical tides and large surf with storm surge may cause moderate flooding in low lying areas along the Redwood/Mendocino Coast. Up to one foot of saltwater inundation above ground level is possible in low lying areas near shorelines and tidal waterways. * WHERE...Coastal Del Norte, Southwestern Humboldt and Coastal Mendocino Counties. * WHEN...From Tuesday morning through Thursday afternoon during periods of high tide. * IMPACTS...Several coastal roads may be closed. Low lying property and some critical infrastructure will be inundated. Some shoreline erosion may occur. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Expect continued increases in high tide water levels through the coming work week with the tide peaking on Wednesday. Prepare now and pay attention to official guidance on shelters and or resources available to the public.

events.title: High Surf Advisory
events.description: * WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, minor coastal flooding. For the Coastal Flood Warning, significant coastal flooding expected. For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 6-8 feet, sets up to 10-12 feet along west-facing beaches. * WHERE...San Diego County Coastal Areas. * WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 4 AM PST Tuesday. For the Coastal Flood Warning, from 4 AM Tuesday to 1 PM PST Friday. For the High Surf Advisory, from 1 PM Wednesday to 4 AM PST Friday. Most susceptible time of flooding will be around the time of the morning high tide, with peak tides trending from 7 AM on Tuesday to 10 AM on Friday. * IMPACTS...Numerous roads may be closed. Low lying property including homes, businesses, and some critical infrastructure will be inundated. Some shoreline erosion will occur. Dangerous swimming and surfing conditions and localized beach erosion. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...King tides peak Tuesday through Wednesday at 7.9-8.3 feet, likely breaking the all-time tidal records set back in late October. Background surf on top of the tides will remain around 2-5 feet through Wednesday morning, but a long period west swell arrives Wednesday afternoon, bringing a sharp increase to the surf for late Wednesday into Thursday. Surf lowers to 5-7 feet by Friday morning's high tide.

weather.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued November 23 at 10:56AM PST until November 24 at 4:00AM PST by NWS San Diego CA
weather.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, minor coastal flooding.
For the Coastal Flood Warning, significant coastal flooding
expected.

* WHERE...Orange County Coastal Areas.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 4 AM PST Tuesday.
For the Coastal Flood Warning, from 4 AM Tuesday to 1 PM PST
Friday. Most susceptible time of flooding will be around the
time of the morning high tide, with peak tides trending from 7
AM on Tuesday to 10 AM on Friday.

* IMPACTS...Numerous roads may be closed. Low lying property
including homes, businesses, and some critical infrastructure
will be inundated. Some shoreline erosion will occur.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...King tides peak Tuesday through Wednesday
at 7.9-8.3 feet, likely breaking the all-time tidal records set
back in late October. Background surf on top of the tides will
remain around 2-5 feet through Wednesday, but a long period west
swell arriving late Wednesday will bring larger surf by Thursday
morning's high tide. Breaking waves may reach 4-6 feet with
local sets up to 7-8 feet on west-facing beaches. Surf lowers
to 3-5 feet by Friday morning's high tide.
weather.instruction:
Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone property. If
travel is required, do not drive around barricades or through
water of unknown depth.

events.title: Coastal Flood Watch
events.description: * WHAT...One to two feet of inundation above ground level possible in low-lying areas near shorelines and tidal waterways. * WHERE...Ocean, Atlantic, Coastal Atlantic, Coastal Ocean and Southeastern Burlington. * WHEN...From Thursday morning through late Thursday night. * IMPACTS...At this level, widespread roadway flooding occurs in coastal and bayside communities and along inland tidal waterways. Many roads become impassable. Some damage to vulnerable structures may begin to occur. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Confidence is high on at least moderate tidal flooding occurring with Thursday morning's high tide. Tide levels could potentially reach the major threshold. Stay tuned to the latest forecast for any changes.

location.region: Ocean; Atlantic; Coastal Atlantic; Coastal Ocean; Southeastern Burlington

weather.headline: Coastal Flood Watch issued November 23 at 1:45PM EST until November 27 at 3:00AM EST by NWS Mount Holly NJ
weather.description:
* WHAT...One to two feet of inundation above ground level
possible in low-lying areas near shorelines and tidal
waterways.

* WHERE...Ocean, Atlantic, Coastal Atlantic, Coastal Ocean and
Southeastern Burlington.

* WHEN...From Thursday morning through late Thursday night.

* IMPACTS...At this level, widespread roadway flooding occurs in
coastal and bayside communities and along inland tidal
waterways. Many roads become impassable. Some damage to
vulnerable structures may begin to occur.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Confidence is high on at least moderate
tidal flooding occurring with Thursday morning's high tide. Tide
levels could potentially reach the major threshold. Stay tuned
to the latest forecast for any changes.
weather.instruction:
A Coastal Flood Watch means that conditions favorable for
flooding are expected to develop.

Be prepared to begin taking appropriate action to protect life
and property. Follow the recommendations of local emergency
management officials. Be sure to check the latest forecast from
time to time in case a warning is issued or any new information
becomes available.

Visit the National Water Prediction Service at
https://water.noaa.gov/wfo/phi for additional water level and
flood impact information for your local tide gauge.
weather.areaDesc: Ocean; Atlantic; Coastal Atlantic; Coastal Ocean; Southeastern Burlington

events.title: Flood Watch
events.description: * WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is possible. * WHERE...A portion of northwest Washington, including the following county, Mason. * WHEN...From Wednesday morning through Sunday afternoon. * IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS... - A series of storms will bring roughly 3 to 6 inches of rainfall to the southern slopes of the Olympics through Thursday with snow levels rising to around 5000 to 5500 feet on Tuesday, and as high as 6000 to 6500 feet on Wednesday. The combination of heavy rain and relatively high snow levels is expected to push the Skokomish River near Potlach above flood stage by midweek. - http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,

weather.headline: Freeze Warning issued November 23 at 11:24AM CST until November 25 at 9:00AM CST by NWS Fort Worth TX
weather.description:
* WHAT...Sub-freezing temperatures as low as 27 expected.

* WHERE...Areas along and west of a line from Gainesville to Fort
Worth to Meridian to Lampasas.

* WHEN...From 11 PM Tuesday to 9 AM CST Wednesday.

* IMPACTS...Frost and freeze conditions could kill crops, other
sensitive vegetation and possibly damage unprotected outdoor
plumbing.
weather.instruction:
A Freeze Warning means that the season's first episode of
sub-freezing temperatures are likely to occur. These conditions will
kill sensitive plants, and residents are advised to protect tender
vegetation. Automatic sprinkler systems should also be turned off to
avoid creating ice patches on nearby roads, driveways, and sidewalks.

Take steps now to protect tender plants from the cold.

events.description: ...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida... For the St. Johns River...including Astor...Major flooding is forecast. * WHAT...Major flooding is occurring and major flooding is forecast. * WHERE...St Johns River near Astor. * WHEN...Until further notice. * IMPACTS...At 4.5 feet, Major widespread and long duration flooding occurs, with water rescues and evacuations necessary. Areas off of Riveredge Drive are inaccessible. Water surrounds and enters homes on Riverview Drive and Claire Street. events.title: Marine Weather Statement
events.description: RISK OF BREAKING WAVES IN THE MORRO BAY AND VENTURA HARBOR ENTRRANCES EARLY WEDNESDAY MORNING THROUGH THURSDAY AFTERNOON A large and long period westerly swell will produce a risk of breaking waves in the Morro Bay and Ventura Harbor entrances early Wednesday morning through Thursday afternoon. These conditions have a history of capsizing vessels of various sizes resulting in serious injury or death, even to the most experienced mariners. Mariners are urged to stay clear of these harbor entrances during the time mentioned. For more information, contact the local harbor patrol or coast guard station and continue to monitor NOAA Weather Radio for the latest weather information.

events.title: Special Weather Statement
events.description: Kilauea eruption episode 57 began at 12:15 AM HST this morning. Lava fountain heights within Halemaumau Crater are currently estimated at a few hundred feet high. The latest radar imagery has detected small volcanic particles as high as 14,500 feet. Light northerly surface winds near the volcano will push low level particles towards the south of the crater. Winds aloft above the low level boundary layer will blow from the northeast direction pushing tephra towards the southwest direction. We will continue to coordinate with USGS scientists on local ashfall impacts as this latest Kilauea eruption and volcanic plume continues to evolve over time. Avoid excessive exposure to ash which is an eye and respiratory irritant. Those with respiratory sensitivities should take extra precaution to minimize exposure.
